name: Ostwald Ripening
desc: An emulsion coarsening under the objective: curvature makes small droplets more soluble than large ones, so the big quietly eat the small, drifting drops coalesce on contact, and every dissolved droplet hands its mass back to the matrix until the supersaturation fires off a fresh burst of nucleation - a dispersion that cycles forever instead of settling; rendered as a lit emulsion micrograph, luminous refracting rims in dark field, a grey phase-contrast plate, or ironbow thermal.

energy.doc: lighting contrast and specular gain on the droplets

scale.doc: magnification into a sub-region of the field - guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: ripening rate - how fast droplets grow, dissolve and drift (0.2 still evolves)

density.doc: volume fraction of the dispersed phase - droplet count and coverage

drift.doc: brownian wander + slow shear of the matrix, which drives coalescence

grain.doc: mottling of the continuous phase and film tooth

hue.doc: hue of the dispersed droplets; the matrix takes a cool complement

x.doc: pan across the field when magnified

y.doc: pan down the field when magnified

style.doc: aesthetic: lit emulsion micrograph / luminous rims on black / grey phase-contrast halos / ironbow false-colour

seed.doc: deterministic initial dispersion and matrix mottling
